messages:
incidents-bot: [ALERT] realtime/streaming: elevated chunking latency detected in us-west-2 (p95 ~ 450ms, p99 ~ 3.8s) for SSE/Websocket responses. Auto-page to #incidents and on-call. Links: <https://grafana.redwood.company/d/streaming-latency|grafana:streaming-latency>
lauren: pinging oncall.sam — saw a spike at 12:07 UTC, lots of 502->retry traces and client backpressure in the proxy. customer-facing errors reported by payments-ingest pipeline. @sam can you take first touch?
sam: on call, grabbing traces. initial read: proxy write queue skyrocketed around 12:06, downstream workers stayed healthy. suspect proxy-to-backend pacing + client slow consumers. grabbing logs and qsize now.
mike: fyi i've got a couple customers reporting UI stutters; they see partial payloads then long pauses. Looks like chunking delays rather than full disconnects.
sam: metric snippets: p95=450ms, p99=3.8s (SSE endpoints), overall request rate normal. See grafana panel. Trying `kubectl exec` into one proxy pod to dump socket stats.
lauren: tagging @eva-cs — CS: any high-severity customers seeing data loss? we should prepare comms if this hits SLAs.
eva-cs: One enterprise customer (AcmeCorp) reported 8 incidents in last 10 mins where data arrived in delayed chunks. They're waiting for ETA. I'll queue a note and ask for impact scope — notifying account exec.
sam: log snippet from proxy (tail):

```
[12:06:12] WARN chunk_delay_ms=1200 conn=1045 writeback_queue=987
[12:06:13] WARN chunk_delay_ms=2450 conn=1121 writeback_queue=1203
[12:06:14] ERROR client_write_timeout conn=1121 err=write: broken pipe
[12:06:15] WARN chunk_delay_ms=3800 conn=998 writeback_queue=1502
```

sam: queue length correlation is strong. Also seeing many clients advertise small window size (slow consumers). Hypothesis: sudden influx of slow consumers causing proxy buffer blowout and tail latency.
raj: two immediate mitigation options: 1) enforce aggressive keepalive/idle timeouts + increase proxy worker count to restore headroom, 2) temporarily route streaming traffic to the dedicated streaming pool in us-east-1 (fallback) while we drain bad connections. I'd prefer 1 first for minimal customer reroute.
mike: +1 for scale + keepalive. How fast can we scale replicas? ops-bot can we spin up more proxy pods + bump per-pod write buffer cap?
ops-bot: running command: `kubectl -n prod scale deployment streaming-proxy --replicas=6` — started. Rolling update in progress. Will report pod readiness.
ops-bot: rollout status: 3/6 new pods ready, 6/6 total ready by 12:12 UTC. No failures observed.
sam: after scaling, p95 down to ~220ms, p99 down to ~1.1s on one panel — still seeing tailers on specific connections. Recommending short-lived aggressive TCP keepalive and reduce max-queue-per-conn to shed slow consumers.
lauren: what's the config change? paste the snippet.
sam: proposed proxy config patch (hot reload supported):

```yaml
streaming:
  conn_max_buffer_bytes: 256000 # reduce from 1MB
  conn_idle_timeout_ms: 45000 # reduce from 120s
  write_backpressure_threshold: 1024
```

sam: i'll apply on one canary proxy pod first.
mike: please tag me when canary is up. If that works we can roll to all pods quickly.
ops-bot: applied patch to pod streaming-proxy-7a2b (canary). Hot reload succeeded.
sam: canary metrics show 80% reduction in per-conn queue and p99 on that pod dropped to 420ms. Good signal.
lauren: roll to all when ready. Also assign oncall handoff: @sam will continue diagnostics for ~20m, then hand to @mike for 1hr follow-up (customer comms + RCA start). Sam please post handoff when ready.
sam: rolling to remaining pods now.
ops-bot: rolling config update: 5/5 pods updated. All proxies show new config.
mike: watching production panels. p95 ~180ms, p99 ~610ms across us-west-2 now. Still some residual clients with multiple reconnects; CS is pulling affected customer IDs.
\
lauren: did we identify any upstream deploy or change that could've triggered slow consumers?
sam: not from our deploys. No new deploys in the last 6 hours. Network blips between CDN edge and proxy? checking network telemetry.
raj: if network is noisy, keepalive + conn buffer shrink is correct fallback. Also recommend enabling automatic short-lived circuit-breakers for connections that exceed X consecutive chunk delays to prevent head-of-line blocking.
mike: agree, file an action item to add circuit-breaker rule: if conn chunk_delay_ms > 2s for 5 chunks -> force-close. We'll validate heuristics in staging.
lauren: CS update?
eva-cs: AcmeCorp seeing reduced incidents after the roll. They've accepted interim reply and asked for postmortem. I'll schedule a call with them 1pm PT. No data lost — just delayed chunks.
sam: handoff: i'm handing the incident to @mike at 12:25 UTC. i'll remain available for escalation. Current state: mitigated — scaling + config reduced p99 by >80%. Next steps: RCA, add circuit-breaker, add improved telemetry for per-conn queue depth, and run a small load test with simulated slow consumers.
mike: taking over. creating an incident ticket with timeline and will start RCA doc. Thanks @sam and team. :thumbsup:
lauren: summary for ops log: short-lived spike in slow consumers led to proxy write queue growth and chunking latencies. Mitigations: scaled proxy replicas, reduced per-conn buffer and idle timeouts, rolled config. Customer impact: partial chunk delays for a handful of customers (no data loss). Owner: mike for RCA. ETA for initial RCA draft: EOD today.
incidents-bot: Incident acknowledged and marked "mitigated" at 12:28 UTC. Please attach RCA link when available.
